visualReview.notes: Inspected every listed frame after the portico correction: parallel cupola ribs and roof lights, lower colonnade, entrance on the correct opposite end from the wide rear wings, double-order tempietto, circular galleries, upper spire and current star are intact. Portico and upper pediment oculi are visible; the distant camera now includes the entire silhouette.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All shared-material angles and named detail frames were inspected. Limestone, slate and metal resolve with metric repeats; curved cupola ribs, granite eyes and deep column recesses remain legible. North-up orthographic placement overlay confirms the corrected portico on the narrow projection and broad rear wings on the opposite mapped end.

geographicReview.notes: The current orthographic placement frame was checked against exact-QID OSM way 83111423. Directed entrance/rear-wing asymmetry, native dimensions, center, rotation and Y=0 terrain-contact base agree at world-viewer exterior scale. This approves the geographic placement represented by the hashed entry; surrounding street paving is separate map scenery.

fidelityReview.notes: Reviewed the complete exterior at all current named near/far and turntable cameras against the Turin museum photographs and contemporary engineering dimensions. The cupola rib/light pattern, lower temple frontage, portico and wide rear wings, two-order tempietto, circular galleries, spire and current star are individually authored and visually coherent. Small carved capitals, pediment sculpture and iron fittings use the catalog’s original polygonal reconstruction style; they are stated reconstruction limits, not missing major exterior assemblies. No interior or survey/photogrammetry requirement is imposed.
